verdict:
Navin's verdict on the opening (28 November 2026). Two changes, and nothing else changes:

1. Point 0-k16. The line "Carbon dioxide mein bhi carbon hai, phir bhi use organic compound nahi gina jaata." gives the exam point without its why. Right after it, add the why in one or two short sentences, in the heading's own voice, the reason a teacher gives a Class 11 learner: organic compounds have carbon joined to hydrogen (usually in a chain), while CO2 has none, so CO2 (like carbonates) is counted as inorganic. Keep it true and simple.

2. Point 0-k9. "Ab van Helmont ki mitti ke woh 57 gram samajh aate hain. Paudhe ne mitti se zyadatar yahi thode minerals liye the." is a teacher's guess, not a sure fact. Navin: "Dhyan wali baat mein shayad kehna jyada sahi rahega." Say it with "shaayad" (those 57 grams may also hold some error of weighing); keep the point that a plant takes only a few minerals from the soil.

Navin also said: the number of words the opening opens is fine for the learner ("bache ke liye itna theek hai"), and every outside-the-book addition stays ("sab rakhein").

lines_removed: Ab van Helmont ki mitti ke woh 57 gram samajh aate hain. Paudhe ne mitti se zyadatar yahi thode minerals liye the.
lines_added: Ab van Helmont ki mitti ke woh 57 gram shaayad samajh aate hain. Paudhe ne mitti se shaayad yahi thode minerals liye the, aur kuch farq tolne ki chook ka bhi ho sakta hai.

Kyunki organic compounds mein carbon hydrogen se juda hota hai, aksar carbon ki kadi bana kar. Carbon dioxide mein carbon ke saath ek bhi hydrogen nahi, isliye ise carbonates ki tarah inorganic gina jaata hai.
